title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext, incl. appendices A-E)
why_wsp: Claude Opus 5.5 writes (and optionally restructures) a small NN's architecture and weights as JSON from a PDE specification, then refines the weights from external physics-loss feedback, with no gradient optimization.
domain: scientific ML: 1D time-dependent PDE solving (heat, advection, Burgers', Allen-Cahn)
editor: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), high reasoning effort, via Claude Code non-interactive mode without tool access
target: Initial 2x20 tanh MLP, 501 parameters; edited architectures have 4-342 parameters
interface: direct values (weights emitted as JSON; architecture as expression layers + MLP blocks)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (K = 5 refinement rounds; select best of 6 candidates by constraint violations then physics loss)
self_editing: no; LLM writes a separate small PDE network
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: all weights written from scratch; "the generated networks have 4–33 parameters for the heat equation, 4–17 for advection, 104–342 for Burgers’, and 36–52 for Allen–Cahn" (Sec 5.6)

headline_results.quote: PtW achieves a relative L2 error of 4.31 × 10−17 , substantially outperforming all baseline methods
PtW achieves a relative L2 error of 2.00 × 10−17

headline_results.claim: Burgers' rel. L2 lowest but PDE residual higher than PINN
headline_results.quote: PtW achieves the lowest relative L2 error of 1.53 × 10−2 ... However, its PDE residual MSE is substantially higher than that of PINN
increasing the spatial resolution from 256 to 2001 points raises the MSE from 5.45 × 10−2 to 6.6 × 109 , while the PINN MSE changes by less than 20%
PtW achieves a relative L2 error of 3.53 × 10−2 , outperforming PINN, WSP, and WSP-PC. ... However, PINN achieves a lower PDE residual than PtW
architecture editing is the primary contributor to solution accuracy, whereas physics-constrained prompting and weight refinement mainly improve constraint satisfaction

headline_results.claim: WR on trained PINN weights: LLM discarded them
headline_results.quote: In all three runs, the LLM discarded the PINN weights in the first refinement round and replaced them with an analytical construction

cost.claim: Wall-clock per network incl. all LLM calls (medians); e.g. PtW 76 s heat, 1066 s Burgers'
cost.quote: Time is the wall-clock time per network, including PINN training (PINN, PINN-WR) and all LLM calls; LLM times depend on server load

baselines_and_controls: PINN (Adam 10k steps + L-BFGS, same 501-param architecture and collocation points), plain WSP (one-shot), WSP-PC, WSP-WR, WSP-PC-WR, WSP-PC-AE, PINN-WR (LLM refinement of trained PINN weights).
runs_and_variance: "Each experiment is repeated three times, and the median performance is reported" (Sec 5.1); no variance/spread reported beyond per-run constraint counts (Table 7).
robustness_of_edits: not tested (only evaluation-grid sensitivity of PDE residual for Burgers')
verification: Rule validator for generated architectures; external numerical evaluator (physics loss, constraint checks C1-C5); reference solutions only for evaluation. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Paper notes heat/advection near machine precision comes from embedding known analytical solution structure: "these results do not necessarily demonstrate the ability to generate highly accurate weights for PDEs without known analytical solutions" (Sec 5.8).
limitations_stated: Accuracy on heat/advection relies on known analytical solutions; Burgers' networks have large local derivatives and high, grid-sensitive PDE residuals; only 1D PDEs, a single LLM, three runs per method.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, Nov 2026)
notes_for_survey: B2 application of WSP to PDEs where the LLM also edits architecture (expression layers + MLPs within a 501-param cap); architecture editing, not weight values, accounts for most accuracy gains. Machine-precision results on heat/advection correspond to the LLM encoding closed-form solutions. LLM has no tool access or code execution; feedback comes from an external evaluator.
